svg.title: Can the image build run in this region?
svg.desc: Use an empty staging group dedicated to one template in the same subscription and region as that template. Protect its staged artifacts and delegated identity privileges by reviewing direct and inherited access while preserving required service and cleanup permissions. Isolated Image Builds uses ACI to communicate with build and validation VMs without a direct public-IP connection. Supply neither subnet, only the build VM subnet, or both subnets. When supplying the ACI subnet, both supplied subnets must share a VNet in the build subscription; a separate networking resource group is allowed. These build restrictions do not prevent cross-subscription gallery consumption. For the build-subnet-only option, disable Private Link service network policies on the supplied build subnet while retaining NSG filtering. Separately allow health probes from AzureLoadBalancer on the configured probe port, application traffic from the actual Private Link service NAT addresses to the proxy on TCP 60001 for Linux or 60000 for Windows, and proxy-to-VM access on TCP 22 or 5986 respectively. The probe tag does not allow application traffic; the Private Link service NAT sources are private addresses, not the outbound NAT gateway's public IP. Both supplied subnets use direct ACI-to-VM connectivity without those proxy prerequisites. A supplied ACI subnet needs the supported NAT gateway outbound configuration; this does not put a public IP on the build VM or override NSG rules. Trace template artifact downloads from ACI separately from guest-script downloads. For template artifacts using Storage public-endpoint subnet rules, pair the ACI-subnet firewall rule with a suitable Storage service endpoint. Private endpoints need their separate DNS and routing path, and network access does not replace data authorization. Check policy compatibility for service-created staging Storage and Azure Files separately from customer artifact access, including the documented staging storage account without a firewall. Hold unresolved policy conflicts for the authorized policy owner; do not enable anonymous artifact access. Check DNS, routing, encrypted access, identity, hashes, explicit outbound connectivity, required providers, ACI and VM quotas, and regional capacity.
svg.metadata: Azure service icons are embedded from C:\Azure-Icons. Each symbol records its source file.
svg.text: Can the image build run in this region?
A role assignment does not create a network route. Available quota does not reserve hardware.

g.text: 1. Dedicate a staging group to one template and choose a network path
Staging: empty, one template, same subscription and region.
Protect staged artifacts and identity privileges; review inherited access.
ACI connects to VMs without a direct public-IP path.
and proxy path to the VM.
Build subnet only: extra Private Link/proxy prerequisites
On the build subnet, set privateLinkServiceNetworkPolicies to Disabled; keep NSG filtering.
Health probes: AzureLoadBalancer -> configured probe port.
Application: Private Link NAT IPs -> proxy TCP 60001 (Linux) or 60000 (Windows).
Proxy -> build/validation VM: TCP 22 (Linux SSH) or 5986 (Windows WinRM HTTPS).
No proxy prerequisites when both subnets are supplied.
2. Trace each artifact download from its caller
Check the build or validation VM's subnet
and the identity used by the script.
Supplied ACI subnet: NAT-backed outbound. An NSG allow rule does not supply egress.
ACI outbound: HTTPS 443 and Azure Files 445.
Both subnets supplied: ACI -> VM on TCP 22 (Linux) or 5986 (Windows).
Build subnet only: also configure the Private Link/proxy path above.
Fix the missing route or role. Do not make the container public.
Resolve conflicts with the policy owner.
Check both VM-family quota and ACI quota.
Quota does not reserve regional hardware.
Include build, validation, and consumer tests.

svg.text: Budget for ACI, VMs, disks, and networking. Builds and replication can take hours.
Failed builds, stored replicas, and cross-region transfers can still incur charges.
